exactGap: Isolation today is one Chromium per ChromiumoxideDriver (launched in ensure_browser, chromiumoxide.rs:194-262) with a per-session CDP browser context inside it (396-420); there is no container or microVM boundary per org or session. ensure_browser also relaunches that single shared Chromium, clearing every session's pages, whenever a lease asks for a different launch viewport (194-223, lease.rs:20-23), so concurrent tenants with different viewports can kill each other's runs. sandbox-manager is only a Postgres lease registry for thread/agent code scopes that hands out a sandbox://<id> string and starts nothing (server.go:84-97, lease.go:154), and the Kernel driver is a REST shim that is never registered (kernel.rs:1-20, main.rs:322-340).

constraints: Ingestion Plane must own the browser fleet. Model Plane sandbox-manager is a Space-capability-bound lease registry for code sandboxes (its backend id is pinned by a Control capability decision, server.go:84-107, main.go:60); making Quarry depend on it inverts 'Model proposes, Quarry executes' and drags Space authority into scraping, so that option in the item should be dropped. PinnedEgressProxyEndpoint is deliberately loopback-only (lib.rs:331-360), so a per-container Chromium needs its own proxy sidecar in the same network namespace or an explicit, reviewed relaxation of that type. ZDR: per-session workers must be ephemeral and profile export must stay blocked under ZDR (the gateway already rejects ZDR plus persistent profile, browser.rs:471-474). Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL, so any lease must be keyed by the verified org_id, not by caller input.
approachAdjustment: Split the item. Step 1 (S to M, no fleet): stop the cross-session blast radius by applying viewport per page or context through CDP emulation instead of relaunching the shared browser (chromiumoxide.rs:194-223), and change the compose default of QUARRY_BROWSER_NO_SANDBOX from 1 to 0 (docker-compose.yml:99 disables the Chromium sandbox when the variable is unset, contradicting its own comment at line 97 and .env.example:20); production manifests were not checked. Step 2 (L): add a CDP-connect mode to ChromiumoxideDriver (Browser::connect to a worker WebSocket) and a per-org pool of Chromium worker containers, each with its own pinned-proxy sidecar, all owned by the Ingestion Plane. Step 3 (XL, optional): microVM per session. Do not present the Kernel or Browserless drivers as a shortcut, they are one-shot REST shims. Also note that scrape-path sessions are keyed by host only (browser_driver.rs:139-148), so concurrent same-host browser scrapes from different orgs may share one session_key (INF, not tested).
effortNote: Original L covered only the pool. Real per-org or per-session isolation needs the CDP-connect driver plus a worker fleet and proxy placement. The cheap hardening in Step 1 is S to M and should be split off as its own quick win.
verdictReason: The isolation gap is real and absent, but the item omits two existing defects that matter more in the short term (viewport-triggered relaunch of the shared Chromium; sandbox disabled by the compose default), offers a wrong-plane option (sandbox-manager) and ignores the loopback-proxy invariant. Reword as a staged item with a quick-win first step.

exactGap: No model-driven profile generation, validation loop, per-org profile cache or extract-to-agent escalation exists. The existing ExtractionProfile (contracts.rs:259-300) is executed only for agent step observations when the caller supplies it (agent_routes.rs:818-824, observation.rs:646-650), and its executor is a string scanner: DOM and Accessibility fields support only '#id', '[data-testid=...]' or the first bare tag name, values are single strings, NetworkJson and Visual sources are skipped, and there are no list, attribute or transform operations (observation.rs:2261-2355). The item's budget doubt is partly resolved: observation.rs:3164 is test code, but the HTTP step route enforces only max_steps (agent_routes.rs:446-450) and the run TTL; max_cost_usd is accepted at run start and per-step costs are written to receipts, yet no cumulative cost check runs because AgentLoop::over_budget (agent_loop.rs:154-162) is only mentioned in edge comments, never called.

Quarry calling inference to generate it is currently refused: every Quarry Model Plane feature is OFF by default and model-invoke is granted:false (model_plane_gate.rs:1-14, cross-plane-token-requests.json:40-46), and DEF-QB-T17-PART2 (org-bound, metered path) has no owner. approachAdjustment: Reorder and re-source. (1) Make the executor a usable generation target first: back DOM fields with scraper selectors, add multi-valued items, attribute reads and a small closed set of transforms, and version the schema (M to L); the current format cannot express list pages. (3) Generate the profile on the Model Plane side as a proposed argument when a monitor or source is created, send it to Quarry for validation and storage keyed by (org, URL template, schema hash), and have Quarry return a typed regenerate signal on selector miss or schema-validation failure; this avoids Quarry calling inference while the grant is refused. effortNote: Unchanged at XL, but it now also includes the executor rewrite and missing budget enforcement; do not schedule Phase B before those land.
verdictReason: Absent is confirmed, but the item is not buildable as described: the profile executor is far too weak to be the generation target, the Quarry to Model Plane inference grant is refused, and Phase B has no cost enforcement on the production step route. Keep Phase A as a later, re-sourced item and mark Phase B blocked.

exactGap: integration-corev2 already ships the provider reads this item wants: Google drive.file.content with exportAs=text or Office export (service.go:300, drive_read.go:30-60 and 594-615), Microsoft drive.file.content (service.go:219), GitHub contents.get and readme.get (service.go:348, 366) and list-only Notion databases and pages (service.go:463-466), and the SPA picker reaches the content ops through the gateway allowlist (browse.rs:33-41). Model Plane agents call integration-corev2 directly (integration_tools.rs:1-30) but the agent catalog omits every content op (integration_tools.rs:98-141), so those calls classify as unknown-means-write and need approval (permission/mod.rs:195-218), and any provider result shown to the model is cut at 2000 characters (integration_tools.rs:54, 817-825). Quarry itself has no URL rewrite table, no provider resolver, no transcript or caption format and no /v1/parse, and no Quarry crate references integration-corev2.

constraints: Provider reads must run on the requesting user's own connection: integration-corev2 owns the tokens and Model Plane already reaches it with an Auth Core ingestion-audience token minted per org and session (integration_tools.rs:20-23, 494-540). Quarry has no such path, so a Quarry ProviderResolver would add a new cross-plane service identity that must still carry the end user, and would put provider ACL and ZDR propagation inside the scraper. Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL, so provider ACL metadata must travel with ingested content into the Data Plane, and ZDR must propagate to integration-corev2 and to any stored export. Reusing browser-session cookies for export is excluded by credential isolation; Notion content needs a new integration-corev2 action because pages are list-only.
approachAdjustment: Move provider-URL routing out of Quarry. (1) Add a dedicated read-only document tool at the Model Plane or gateway (URL to provider and file id, then drive.file.content with exportAs=text for Google, drive.file.content for Microsoft, contents.get or readme.get for GitHub) that decodes content to bounded text or stores it in the working set; merely adding catalog rows is not enough because content ops return base64 and the model only sees the first 2000 characters. (2) In Quarry keep only a small public-URL rewrite table (link-shared Google export URLs) whose output goes through the file router. (3) Demote the YouTube or caption transcript format, nothing exists and it needs a cookie-free design. Step 0 answers: no document converter was found under Data Plane v2 services (negative grep); chat attachments convert through the gateway (chat.rs:68, 1 MB and 60k character caps in prepare-chat-attachments.ts) and Quarry has its own docx.rs and pdf.rs, so a Quarry /v1/parse route is not justified without a quality comparison; the integration-corev2 Google and Microsoft content ops are not yet verified against live providers (drive_read.go header, task F10).
effortNote: Unchanged in total, but the bundle should be split: the document tool is S to M, the Quarry rewrite table is S, the transcript format is M and demoted.
verdictReason: The item says integration-corev2 coverage was not inspected; it is substantial, and the real gap is routing plus agent-visible content tools, not new connectors or a Quarry ProviderResolver. Reword to the Model Plane or gateway chokepoint and drop the Quarry to integration-corev2 design.

exactGap: Explicit deadlines exist only for download begin and complete (10 s and 30 s, chromiumoxide.rs:76-77), the 5 s profile-capture wrapper (683-693), caller-bounded waits (1733-1740, 2807) and lease acquisition (lease_pool.rs:124); everything else (navigate, content, evaluate, screenshot, AX snapshot, input, tab open) rides chromiumoxide's library default request_timeout of 30 s because the BrowserConfig builder sets none (226-262; chromiumoxide-0.9.1 handler/mod.rs:34, 681), and failures surface as DriverFailed strings rather than a typed Timeout naming the operation (1988-2004, 2017-2023) while DriverFailed is not retryable (error.rs:38-43). Quarry already fails stale or destroyed-frame ref targets with TargetRepairRequired 'observe again' instead of rebinding (1245-1278, 2100-2140), and the Model Plane already retries transient failures of non-risky tool calls up to three times (runtime_loop/retry.rs:37) but deliberately never retries browser.act or browser_agent (permission/mod.rs:261-271). Agent runs are bounded by max_steps and max_runtime_s only (gateway sets 12 and 120, browser.rs:483-490; agent_routes.rs:446-451).

constraints: Deadlines are Quarry execution policy: per-run overrides may only tighten or stay under a Quarry-side maximum, the Model must not be able to widen them (Model proposes, Quarry executes). Retrying actions is unsafe by design: the Model Plane gates browser.act and browser_agent as risky and the retry helper is risk-gated for the same reason (retry.rs:1-25), and ref-bound actions already fail closed with TargetRepairRequired. ZDR is unaffected; timeouts must not log URLs or page text into details under ZDR.
approachAdjustment: Keep it inside quarry-browser, S in size. Set request_timeout and launch_timeout explicitly on the BrowserConfig builder, add a small deadlines module with one cdp_call(op, fut) wrapper that returns ErrorCode::Timeout with details {op, ms} (and wrap goto, which today maps any failure to DriverFailed), and add retry-once only for idempotent read calls (content, AX snapshot, evaluate) when the error text indicates a destroyed context. Never retry ref or coordinate actions; they keep surfacing TargetRepairRequired. Drop the proposed Model Plane planner rule: Model Plane already retries non-risky transient failures, and browser actions are intentionally excluded. Calibrate deadlines from telemetry rather than copying Codex's numbers. Note the item's evidence line chromiumoxide.rs:685 is the profile-capture timeout, not an accessibility snapshot, and there is no 750 ms AX quiet-window equivalent in Quarry.
effortNote: Unchanged. The Model Plane half of the item disappears, and the library already supplies a 30 s per-command floor.
verdictReason: Partial is right and the quick-win size holds, but the Model Plane planner rule conflicts with the risk-gated retry design, the evidence line for the accessibility timeout is wrong, and the item missed that the library already enforces a 30 s per-command timeout and that DriverFailed is non-retryable. Reword to a quarry-browser-only change.

exactGap: execute_with_retry is exported (lib.rs:164) but only its own tests call it; the live retries are Temporal activity retries (5 attempts, exponential, workflows.go:94-104), which cover job paths only, not sync /v1/scrape or agent routes. PageRunner calls fetch_conditional once while holding the per-host slot (pipeline.rs:335-364), FallbackDriver.fetch_inner walks drivers with no deadline or budget split (fallback_driver.rs:57-120), ScrapeRequest has no timeout field (routes.rs:346-375) and FetchPolicy.timeout_s is declared with a default of 30 but no fetch code reads it (policy.rs:86-103). ErrorCode has 17 coarse codes (error.rs:10-30) and DriverFailed is not retryable (error.rs:38-43), so wiring the existing helper alone would not retry DNS, connect or browser-launch failures, and there is no sub-code or processing-continues detail (api_error.rs carries only retry_after_seconds).

Retries must re-enter the per-host slot or consult the AIMD scheduler rather than sleep inside the slot (pipeline.rs:343-364 holds it across the fetch). The client-supplied timeout is a request from the caller (possibly the Model) that Quarry clamps to its own maximum. approachAdjustment: Reorder: (c) sub-codes first, so DriverFailed{dns|tls|connect|all_drivers_failed} can carry its own retryable flag and robots or policy denials stay non-retryable; (a) then add timeout_ms to scrape and clamp it, with child cancellation tokens per FallbackDriver attempt and a reserved slice for the last tier (the model-gateway already bounds a scrape client-side at 30 s and escalates once to the browser itself, so avoid double budgeting); (b) last, wire execute_with_retry (or a variant taking fetch hints, since it calls driver.fetch without hints) around the sync scrape path only. effortNote: Stays M if sub-codes stay inside Quarry's own envelope; L if they are propagated through Temporal, webhooks, the gateway and Model Plane tool results.
verdictReason: Partial is confirmed. The item misses that DriverFailed is non-retryable (so wiring the helper alone does little), that Temporal already retries job paths (retry multiplication), that FetchPolicy.timeout_s is not enforced anywhere and that the model-gateway already bounds scrapes client-side. Reword with the corrected ordering.

exactGap: /v1/batch is a durable handoff that forwards only urls, ingest, org and user (routes.rs:669-716) to BatchJobWF, which processes URLs in a plain sequential loop (workflows.go:359-381) with no per-batch options, maxConcurrency, append, invalid-URL report or cancel handlers, and the edge exposes no per-job status or cancel route (only /v1/:kind/jobs and /v1/jobs/:id/events, routes.rs:192, 232); durable batch and crawl jobs are refused under ZDR (routes.rs:563-583). The crawl and batch handoff sends no Idempotency-Key at all (handoff.rs:26-82); the random keys at resource_routes.rs:471-474 and schedule_routes.rs:164-171 belong to other forwarded mutations, while control's createJob already returns the existing job for a repeated (org, key) (resources.go:395-450) but its unique index is on idempotency_key alone (migration 007) and the generic route-level handler is a no-op placeholder (cycle23.go:436). exactGap: Capability flags and gates exist (BrowserDriverCapabilities, lib.rs:265-286; require_isolated_agent_egress and require_driver_capabilities, agent_routes.rs:1125-1217, with driver_requirements already accepted at 1305), but the agent path is hard-wired to one driver, state.agent_driver = ChromiumoxideDriver (main.rs:1283-1288), so there is nothing to register Kernel or Browserless into for agent runs; the scrape path has a single DriverKind::Browser slot that Browserbase takes before the local driver (main.rs:322-339). Kernel and Browserless are REST-only one-shot shims (kernel.rs:1-20, browserless.rs:1-12) constructed only in tests, and Browserbase never opens its connectUrl (browserbase.rs:5-12), so none of the three can serve ref-based actions, AX snapshots or live frames. The session API has a hard-coded capability list but no backend listing (browser.rs:2578, 2700), and per-run driver_capabilities are only echoed after a run exists (agent_routes.rs:543, 1658).

constraints: Remote browsers are third-party processors: they need an approved processor policy and are refused under ZDR (privacy.rs tests), plus DPA review. Containment proof conflict: the pinned egress proxy endpoint type is loopback-only (lib.rs:331-360), which a remote browser cannot reach, so 'route provider traffic through Quarry's pinned proxy' contradicts that invariant, and GAP.md:450-462 records that Kernel and Browserbase only offer main-frame allowlists and that a real CDP connection is a prerequisite; the roadmap gate also requires redirect, iframe, XHR and subresource SSRF tests per provider before agent use (WEB_AGENT_ROADMAP_EXECUTION.md:85-89). Model proposes capability requirements and Quarry selects or rejects; the Model must never name a provider, and no driver_requirements usage was found in Model Plane Rust or Go sources.
approachAdjustment: Re-scope into three parts. (1) S to M, scrape path only: allow more than one managed browser driver by keying the registry beyond DriverKind::Browser (main.rs:322-339) and register Kernel or Browserless behind config with the existing managed_provider processor guard; this adds page-render burst capacity without touching agent governance. (2) XL for agent sessions: build a CDP-attached remote driver that reuses ChromiumoxideDriver over Browser::connect (the REST shims cannot do ref actions), replace the single state.agent_driver with a registry keyed by backend id, then implement and test the containment proof; keep Browserbase scrape-only until then. (3) S: expose GET /v1/agent/backends with capability sets and select by driver_requirements in start_run. Restrict managed providers to approved processor policies and non-ZDR runs.
effortNote: The item assumed the Kernel and Browserless drivers were ready to register. They are REST shims, so agent-capable remote backends need a new CDP-attached driver, a driver registry in AppState and a real containment proof.
verdictReason: Partial and already planned as a gate, but the central premise (register the implemented Kernel and Browserless drivers) is wrong for agent sessions and the proxy-based proof conflicts with the loopback-only invariant. Reword with the corrected split and a larger agent-session effort.
